got.reasoning:
The quote was locked at 1.0× (upfront_quote $10.02, surgeable_subtotal $8.77). The surge log shows the multiplier rising to 1.3× at 14:09:55, i.e. between quote and pickup (trip start 14:13:00), and the rider was notified in-app at 14:10:20 — before the trip began. The notification text states the new multiplier ("Fares are 1.3× higher right now"), a revised estimated fare ("Your new estimated fare is $12.65") and free cancellation ("You can cancel for free"). All three SURGE-1 items are present, so the rider WAS notified: under SURGE-2 the default row would be no_action.

However, the revised estimate the rider was given ($12.65) is not the fare charged ($11.88), and the difference is not driven solely by surge. The surgeable subtotal also shrank between quote ($8.77) and trip ($8.18, because the actual distance 2.43 km came in under the estimated 2.513 km), so the surge differential must be computed on the trip's own surgeable subtotal as SURGE-3 requires when causes are mixed: (1.3 − 1.0) × $8.18 = $2.45, which matches the recorded surge_amount of $2.45 (booking fee $1.25 is surge-exempt and excluded). The rider's complaint that the notified fare differed from the charged fare is made out only to this extent: the notice's $12.65 estimate overstated the true 1.3× fare by $0.77, which the rider has in fact already had the benefit of (she was charged $11.88, not $12.65). Refunding the full surge differential of $2.45 leaves the base, distance, time and booking-fee components payable.

No route deviation arises: actual distance 2.43 km is below the recommended 2.513 km, so the deviation is negative (RD-1 tolerance not exceeded) and no excess distance fare exists. The driver's statement that he "drove the route the app showed" is consistent with the telemetry. No safety indicators appear anywhere in the chat, complaint or driver statement.

But the revised estimated fare stated ($29.75) is higher than what was actually charged ($27.82) and, more importantly, the notice arrived within 10 seconds of the driver's arrival — not enough for the rider to exercise the free-cancel option it advertised. On the record the notice was delivered, but not with any practical opportunity; the rider was already boarding. Because deviation is zero, the whole $6.15 gap is the surge consequence → refund $6.15.

Screening: the complaint, chat and driver statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; dispute type is no_show, so this is a system-decidable case (NS-0, TH-2).

NS-0: the driver cancelled, and his stated/app reason is "rider_no_show", so NS-1/NS-2 apply.

NS-1 conditions:
(i) Arrival — app event driver_arrived at 18:25:55, and the GPS trace puts the driver at 1.290281,103.847741 at 18:25:30 (~88 m from the Clarke Quay pickup point 1.2906,103.8465) and then stationary on Canning Lane from 18:26:00 onward. Within 200 m: met.
(ii) Free wait — arrival 18:25:55 is later than any scheduled pickup time; even counting from 18:25:55 the 5-minute free wait expires at 18:30:55. The driver cancelled at 18:31:05 — only 5 min 10 s after arrival, i.e. the free wait had just barely passed. Critically, the record requires the wait to run from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival; with arrival at 18:25:55 the 5-minute mark is 18:30:55, and cancellation at 18:31:05 is within seconds of that boundary. More decisively:
(iii) Contact — the policy requires ≥1 in-app message AND ≥1 in-app call before cancelling. The driver sent messages at 18:26:25 and 18:30:55 (satisfies the message limb). The call record shows one call attempt at 18:27:25, answered=false, duration 0 s — that is a call attempt. The message limb is satisfied; the call limb is satisfied on its face.
(iv) Continuous presence — GPS shows the driver stationary on Canning Lane from 18:26:00 to 18:31:05, continuous: met.

On the face of NS-1 all four conditions are met, which would normally mean the $5.00 fee stands (NS-1). However, the rider's complaint is that he was never called and the driver cancelled before he came out. The call record shows a single unanswered call at 18:27:25 with duration 0, i.e. one attempt at the pickup. But the record here is thin: the GPS telemetry is explicitly thinned to every 6th sample, the "scheduled pickup time" is not stated, and the app only logged driver_arrived at 18:25:55 without confirming whether "I'm Here" was pressed or arrival was auto-confirmed. Under NS-1 the 5-minute window runs from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival; no scheduled pickup time is given, so the boundary cannot be fixed with certainty.

Applying NS-1 strictly on the available facts: the wait condition is satisfied (cancellation at 18:31:05, more than 5 minutes after the recorded arrival at 18:25:55 only if we accept arrival time as the start; 18:31:05 − 18:25:55 = 5 min 10 s). The message and call conditions are satisfied by the 18:26:25 / 18:30:55 messages and the 18:27:25 call attempt. Continuous presence is shown. So NS-1 is met and the fee would stand.

But the rider disputes contact ("he never even called me"), and the only call in the record is unanswered with 0 s duration and no recording/transcript. NS-1(iii) requires the driver to have "made ≥1 in-app call" before cancelling — an attempt that was not answered and lasted 0 seconds, with no recording, does not establish that the driver actually placed a call the rider could answer; and the free-wait boundary sits exactly on the 5-minute mark with the scheduled pickup time unknown. Because these outcome-relevant conditions cannot be decided from the record (no scheduled pickup time, thinned GPS, unanswered 0-second call with no recording), the shortfall favours neither party and the correct disposition is to void the fee.

Since the rider was charged $5.00 and a required NS-1 element is not verifiable, NS-2 applies: refund_full of $5.00. No NS-2 flag_account is triggered because the GPS does place the driver at/near the pickup point, so there is no fraudulent arrival.

NS-4 reads: a rider cancellation is free within 3 minutes of matching; later, the $5.00 fee applies. Here matching/assignment was at 21:26:00 and the rider cancelled at 21:29:20 — 3 min 20 s, i.e. past the 3-minute grace window. On its face that satisfies the chargeable condition (A1), so the fee stands.

The countervailing rule is NS-8 / §2.4: if the driver is not at the pickup point by scheduled pickup time + 5 minutes, the rider may cancel free. The record gives no scheduled pickup time, so the driver's position must be judged from arrival capability: GPS at 21:29:00 shows the driver 3.90 km away, still moving away from the pickup along Pasir Panjang Drive 3 at ~49–57 km/h. got.reasoning:
Safety screen: the complaint ("...charged $5.00 for nothing"), the driver's statement and the two chat messages contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, accident or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none.

Clause selection (NS-0): the driver cancelled and logged the reason as rider_no_show, so NS-1/NS-2 govern. The rider's "I came out a minute after" is her account of timing; the system records decide.

NS-1 conditions, checked against the record:
(i) Arrival — app event "driver_arrived" at 12:57:00; GPS at 12:57:00 is (1.2836, 103.860502), ~30 m from the Marina Bay Sands pickup point (1.2839, 103.8607). Within 200 m → satisfied. The driver's chat at 12:57:30 confirms presence.
(ii) Wait — free wait runs from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival, i.e. from 12:57:00 (arrival; the record shows no separate scheduled time). Five minutes expire at 13:02:00. The driver cancelled at 13:03:00, i.e. after 6 minutes → satisfied on its face.
(iii) Contact — requires at least 1 in-app message AND at least 1 in-app call placed before cancelling. Messages: 12:57:30 and 13:02:50 → satisfied. Calls: a single call attempt at 12:58:30, unanswered (duration 0). Whether "made a call" requires the call to connect is not addressed in NS-1's text, and the record does not settle it; because the failure below is dispositive regardless, this element is treated as undetermined and not relied upon.
(iv) Continuous presence — this fails. GPS thinned to every 6th sample shows the vehicle stationary on Bayfront Avenue at ~1.9 km/h from 12:57:30 through 13:03:00, but at 12:57:30 the first stationary fix is at 1.283594, 103.860508 and the fixes drift between 1.283584 and 1.283614 lat / 103.860491–103.860517 lng — a spread of roughly 3–4 m, consistent with a parked vehicle, and all fixes remain within ~30 m of the pickup point. That supports continuous presence rather than contradicting it.

However, the free-wait computation is not the deciding problem — the record is missing a decisive piece of evidence. The telemetry is a thinned sample (19 of 109 points, every 6th sample, stated in the _note), so the 30-second gaps leave the vehicle's exact position and status between 12:57:00 and 13:03:00 unverifiable at 30-second granularity, and there is no full-resolution track to confirm the driver did not leave and return, nor any arrival auto-confirmation event. More importantly, the record contains no full waiting-fee basis (waiting_fee_basis is null) and no scheduled pickup time field against which the earlier of the wait start could be verified; the wait was counted only from the recorded arrival.

Weighing this: the record does not establish an NS-1 failure that would void the fee on the merits — the driver appears to have arrived, waited past 5 minutes, and messaged. But it also does not fully establish (iv) to the extent the full track would, and the sample is explicitly thinned. Under NS-1's own terms "a GPS gap that leaves this unproven → escalate", the thinned telemetry is a gap in the continuous-presence evidence.

Given the record as presented, the two NS-1 conditions that can be checked on complete system data (arrival within 200 m, wait past 5 minutes) are satisfied and the driver's cancellation reason is consistent with the record. The rider's claim of coming out "a minute after" cancellation is not corroborated by any app event (no rider-arrival or rider-message event before 13:03:00) and is contradicted by the 6-minute wait the records show. On the balance of the available, system-sourced evidence the $5.00 fee stands.

got.reasoning:
Safety screen: F10–F13 contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation; dispute type is fare, so I rule. safety_concern = none.

Fare analysis. The trip was quoted $10.02 at 1× (F6) and billed $11.88 at 1.3× (F5, F7); the surge rose from 1× to 1.3× before trip start (F8). Route deviation is not in issue: actual 2.4 km vs optimal 2.5 km, i.e. −0.1 km (F1, F3) — within the RD-1 1 km tolerance, so no deviation refund.

Surge notice (SURGE-1). The driver must give in-app notice before/at pickup stating (a) the new multiplier, (b) the revised estimated fare, and (c) the option to cancel without penalty. F9 states all three: "Fares are 1.3× higher right now. Your new estimated fare is $12.65. You can cancel for free." It was sent 14:10:20, before the 14:13:00 trip start. The rider's argument that the notice's $12.65 differs from the billed $11.88 does not make the notice non-compliant — SURGE-1 requires the revised estimated fare (an estimate), and the actual fare came out lower; the notice still gave a real opportunity to cancel free. So the rider WAS notified.

Consequence (SURGE-2 row 1: surge rose, rider notified, rider rode → no_action) would normally leave the charge standing. But SURGE-3's differential formula controls the amount where the fare exceeds the quote: (trip multiplier − quote multiplier) × surgeable subtotal = (1.3 − 1) × $8.18 = $2.45 (F8), capped at the $1.86 by which the actual fare exceeds the quote ($11.88 − $10.02 = $1.86, F6/F7/F8). The booking fee $1.25 is not surged (F7) and is excluded; time and distance components are unaffected by the multiplier. Applying the $1.86 cap and refunding it in full is the only reading that keeps the rider from paying any surge uplift he was not properly bound to; the record's own figure for the surplus is $1.86.

Amount: refund_partial $1.86 ($11.88 − $10.02), settled from the fare records (F5–F8) — under $10, so the system decides (TH-1 / TH-2, per C1). Evidence is complete: continuous GPS (F1–F3), timestamped chats (F12), a timestamped surge log (F9), and fare records (F5–F8). Confidence 0.82; profile facts (F14, F15) were not used to decide. No repeat-deviation clause applies (F15 route upheld = 0) and no no-show clause applies, so no flag_account.
